sections.title: Basic Concept of Reading Comprehension
sections.content: In Reading Comprehension, a short passage is given and questions are asked based on it. At Level 1, the questions are directly based on the information provided in the passage. The student needs to read carefully and identify the main idea and important facts.

sections.title: Direct Factual Questions
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the keywords given in the question. Step 2: Search for the same word or its similar meaning in the passage. Step 3: Choose the answer directly from that sentence. Example: In questions starting with 'According to the passage...', the answer is usually written in the passage itself.

sections.title: Main Idea of the Passage
sections.content: Step 1: Carefully read the first and the last sentence of the passage. Step 2: Identify the idea that appears repeatedly throughout the passage. Step 3: The option that summarizes this idea briefly will be the correct main idea.

sections.title: Title Selection
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the main topic of the passage. Step 2: Check which option represents the entire passage. Step 3: Avoid titles that are too narrow or too broad. The correct title is the one that summarizes the whole passage.

sections.title: Vocabulary Based Questions
sections.content: Step 1: Read the sentence in which the word appears in the passage. Step 2: Understand its meaning in that context. Step 3: Choose the synonym or antonym from the options that best fits the context of the passage.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Guessing the answer without reading the passage. 2. Selecting answers by only looking at the options. 3. Choosing the general meaning in vocabulary questions when the contextual meaning is different.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Reading Comprehension, first understand the passage and then read the questions. Direct questions usually have answers in the passage, the main idea represents the overall summary of the passage, and vocabulary meanings should be understood from the context.

tricks.title: Keyword Search Trick
tricks.explanation: Quickly search the main keyword from the question in the passage.
tricks.example: If the question contains the word 'environment', look for that word in the passage.

tricks.title: First and Last Sentence Trick
tricks.explanation: The main idea is often found in the first or last sentence.
tricks.example: The introduction and conclusion help identify the main topic.

tricks.title: Scan and Locate Method
tricks.explanation: Instead of rereading the entire passage, locate the relevant part quickly.
tricks.example: Find the paragraph related to the question.

tricks.title: Context Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: Understand the meaning of vocabulary from the context of the sentence.
tricks.example: The phrase 'bright student' may mean an intelligent student.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: First eliminate the options that are clearly incorrect.
tricks.example: Remove options that do not match the passage.

tricks.title: Title Balance Trick
tricks.explanation: The title should neither be too narrow nor too broad.
tricks.example: If the passage is about wildlife, the title 'Animals' would be too broad.

tricks.title: According to Passage Rule
tricks.explanation: In such questions, rely only on the information given in the passage.

tricks.title: Repeated Idea Trick
tricks.explanation: The idea that appears repeatedly is usually the main idea.
tricks.example: If several sentences discuss pollution, then pollution is the main topic.
